scope: Completed retrieval and comparison of every D17 bullet, including its named audit holds and the separate Constellation target decision, plus Illinois first and the authorised Ulam follow-up. No records admitted or corrected; no editorial decisions applied. No changes to data/, src/, release/ or review/. No PR, merge, main push, publication or deployment.
method: Cited review sections read before retrieval. Primary sources retrieved sequentially by direct curl HTTP with at least 1.5 seconds between requests; archive fallback where needed. Source bodies kept in memory only, except the authorised unedited Illinois government-edict extraction. Short quotations and authored comparisons only. HTTP 200 is not treated as proof of a document. Capture timestamps distinguish preserved expressions from event/publication dates. No Wikipedia evidence. English renderings of Chinese are machine translations, not human verified. HTTP failures were retried outside the sandbox network allowlist. Search-engine discovery was used for source locations only; comparisons rest on the directly retrieved sources listed below. Temporary scan page images were used for visual reading and are not retained in the worktree. For the original 29-item batch, all PDF pages were extracted where a text layer was available; comparisons use the identified passages, headings and content boundaries, not an exhaustive clause-by-clause collation or a check of mathematical results. Ulam follow-up: PDF pp. 1 and 5 were extracted, and p. 5 was also read visually; the rest of the memoir was not audited.

items.title: O10 earlier orbital lead: ASPLOS 2020
items.review: review/cpo-admission-1-2026-10-30.md § Held; § Open for the maintainer 1; current data/entities.json O10 criterion and src/reading/orbital-compute.ts role note read for comparison
items.held_point: Read the earlier orbital-edge paper for workload limits imposed by ground links.

sources.quote: Limits on downlink bitrate prevent bent pipes from scaling to accommodate the extreme data volumes of large constellations
sources.locator: Section 1, PDF p. 2, paragraph beginning Challenges faced by existing systems
sources.paraphrase: Bradley Denby and Brandon Lucia, Orbital Edge Computing: Nanosatellite Constellations as a New Class of Computer System. Abstract and introduction tie ground-station access, intermittent downlinks and latency to Earth-observation workloads, proposing onboard processing; p. 1 prints ASPLOS 2020, 16–20 March.

items.comparison: The 2020 paper explicitly connects downlink limits to Earth-observation data volumes and motivates computing on the satellite.
